characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni microstructure consists of two phases: bright white B2 particles decorating grain boundaries and grain interiors of the grey γ matrix (Fig. 1c,d).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: As-cast plus homogenised and hot-rolled samples; RD-ND plane
characterization_methods.purpose: General microstructural observation of the hot-rolled alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI SEM with EDAX EBSD detector; EDAX TSL-OIM v8 software
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni hot-rolled: equiaxed polygonal grains; B2 phase fraction ~4%; twin fraction ~40%; average grain size 6.9 ± 1.7 μm; γ-matrix texture near-random (Fig. 2c,d).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Large-area scans 500×500 μm² with 0.2 μm step; high-resolution scans 100×100 μm² with 0.1 μm step; RD-ND plane; GOS cut-off of 2° for recrystallisation fraction; σ3 (CSL) boundaries for twin fraction
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate grain orientations, phase fractions, grain size, twin boundary fraction and recrystallisation
characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscattered diffraction / Orientation imaging microscopy (EBSD/OIM)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku smart lab X-ray diffractometer; cobalt Kα radiation, 135 mA current, 40 kV voltage
characterization_methods.key_findings: Confirms formation of the B2 phase in the γ-matrix in the Ni-added alloys (28Mn5Ni, 15Mn5Ni).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tecnai 20T G2 (FEI) TEM operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: In 28Mn5Ni alloy, B2 particles of ~300 nm are located at γ-grain boundaries (Fig. 3b); κ-carbides are present (dark-field images).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Hot-rolled samples; twin-jet electropolished thin foils
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine detailed microstructural features (B2 particles, κ-carbides, twins, DO3 reflections)
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (bright-field, dark-field and SAED)

characterization_methods.key_findings: In 28Mn5Ni: γ-matrix Fe-27.8Mn-7.5Al-5.7Ni and B2 Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni (wt%); no compositional gradients within B2 grains; clear solute partitioning between γ and B2.
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse the composition of the phases (γ matrix and B2)

characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni macrohardness is HV268 ± 5; nickel addition has only a marginal effect on hardness.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ASTM E140-02; average of ten readings at random locations
characterization_methods.purpose: Macrohardness measurement of the hot-rolled samples

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, initial strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1, ASTM E8M cylindrical specimens (gauge diameter 6 mm, gauge length 30 mm); RD orientation; elongation measured by punch marks and extensometer; three samples per condition
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate the tensile behaviour of the hot-rolled alloys

characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn5Ni exhibits a dimpled, fibrous fracture surface with microvoid coalescence and cup-and-cone geometry (ductile failure).
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine fracture surfaces after tensile testing

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimate the yield strength of the recrystallised austenite
analytical_models.model_name: Hall-Petch equation: σ_y,Rx-aust = σ0 + k_HP · d^(-1/2)
analytical_models.model_note: σ0 and k_HP values were determined from experimental results reported by Etienne et al. for Fe-28.8Mn-9.4Al-0.92C.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical mean-field estimate using the Hall-Petch relationship
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The estimated yield strength of recrystallised austenite with grain size 5–7 μm (as in the present LDS alloys) is about 460–500 MPa; this is about 170–200 MPa less than the experimentally observed yield strength of the 28Mn0Ni alloy, with the difference attributed to the κ-carbide volume fraction.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation pile-up / strain accumulation at γ/B2 interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Non-shearable B2 particles increase strength via dislocation pile-up; interface orientation determines whether slip is transmitted (favourable OR) or accumulates strain (non-favourable OR).

interfaces.interface_notes: Table 2 shows 28Mn5Ni contains intergranular B2 particles (no B2 stringers, unlike 15Mn5Ni). Detailed OR/slip-transfer analyses (TEM, ACOM) in this study were performed on the 15Mn5Ni alloy; the γ/B2 interface behaviour is here reported as the general conclusion for B2-containing hot-rolled LDS, which includes 28Mn5Ni.

phase_interfaces.coherence: A favourable orientation relationship (OR) between the γ-matrix and B2 facilitates slip transfer while non-favourable OR restricts slip, causing strain accumulation and B2-cracking.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Slip transfer occurs across γ/B2 interfaces with favourable OR, allowing γ-matrix and B2 to co-deform near yield; slip restriction and strain accumulation occur at non-favourable OR interfaces.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Compared with the B2-free hot-rolled 28Mn0Ni alloy (Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) along RD: differences in tensile properties between 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni were minor; the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni exhibited slightly higher strength (YS 730 vs 670 MPa; UTS 1028 vs 980 MPa) and lower ductility (55% vs 68% elongation).

Compared with the B2 stringer-rich hot-rolled 15Mn5Ni alloy: the 15Mn5Ni alloy displayed higher yield/UTS and much lower elongation (20%) than 28Mn5Ni; the 28Mn(0,5)Ni alloys exhibited 55–68% total elongation against 20% for 15Mn5Ni; the hardness and yield strength difference between 28Mn0Ni/28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni is about HV120 and 450 MPa.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Three austenitic LDS grades were prepared by vacuum induction melting route; defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were used.
Defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours.
Hot rolling of the homogenised ingots at 1323 K; total thickness reduction of nearly 85% achieved with ~15% reduction per pass. Same schedule applied to all three LDS grades.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile specimens cut along the rolling direction (RD); three samples tested per condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical tensile specimen, gauge diameter 6 mm, gauge length 30 mm
measurement_conditions.temperature_unit: tensile test figure box states T = 300 K

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 5a: true stress–true strain curve of 28Mn5Ni (RD) is shown; no noticeable plateau near yield; curve extends beyond true strain 0.3, nearly overlapping with 28Mn0Ni

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: 5–7 μm after hot rolling (range reported for the three alloys)
grain_structure.texture: near-random crystallographic texture, similar among the three alloys

phases_present.morphology: fine particles within matrix grains and along grain boundaries

precipitates.distribution: within γ grains and along grain boundaries; 28Mn5Ni shows finer κ-carbides than 15Mn5Ni

phases_present.morphology: intergranular polygonal particles (~300 nm at γ-grain boundaries)
secondary ordered phase associated with B2

precipitates.distribution: within B2 (secondary SAED reflections; [011]B2||[011]DO3 orientation relationship)

structures.overall_structure: Multi-constituent microstructure of a γ (austenite) matrix containing fine κ-carbides, together with intergranular B2 (ordered Fe(Ni)Al) particles and DO3 ordered Fe3Al. Table 2 lists the phases present as γ + κ + intergranular B2 particles + DO3.

unmapped_findings: Analysed chemical composition of the 28Mn5Ni alloy (wt%, Table 1): Mn 28.1, Al 8.6, C 0.9, Ni 4.8, Fe balance.
Phase compositions of hot-rolled 28Mn5Ni (wt%, Table 2): γ-matrix Fe-27.8Mn-7.5Al-5.7Ni; B2 Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni, indicating solute partitioning between γ and B2.
In the 28Mn5Ni alloy, B2 particles of ~300 nm were observed at γ-grain boundaries (yellow arrows, Fig. 3b).
The crystallographic texture of the γ-matrix in the three hot-rolled alloys is similar and near-random.
Nickel addition has only a marginal effect on hardness: the 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni alloys display hardness of HV256 and HV268, respectively.

The B2 phase fraction slightly decreased upon hot rolling at 1323 K (e.g., 15Mn5Ni dropped from ~15% as-cast to ~12% after hot rolling), suggesting possible B2 dissolution; the same hot-rolling schedule (~85% total reduction, ~15% per pass at 1323 K) was applied to all three LDS grades.
The 28Mn5Ni alloy fails predominantly by ductile microvoid coalescence with cup-and-cone fracture geometry and dimples (Fig. 6b), unlike the quasi-cleavage fracture of 15Mn5Ni.
The strain hardening behaviour of the 28Mn5Ni alloy was found to be similar to that of 28Mn0Ni and was not plotted in Fig. 5c for brevity.
